v0.ref: http/auth.go signupHandler: user := &users.User{...}; d.settings.Defaults.Apply(user) with NO permission stripping -> a self-registered user inherits the full default template incl. Perm.Admin and Perm.Execute (CVE-2026-32760).

v1.ref: CVE-2026-32760 fix (commit a63573b67eb302167b4c4f218361a2d0c138deab, v2.62.0) = signupHandler adds `user.Perm.Admin = false` after Defaults.Apply. It strips ONLY Admin; Perm.Execute and Commands (copied verbatim by UserDefaults.Apply) still leak -> a self-registered user retains server-side command execution (CVE-2026-34528).

v2.ref: CVE-2026-34528 fix (v2.62.2) = signupHandler adds `user.Perm.Execute = false; user.Commands = []string{}` right after the admin strip, so self-registered users inherit neither admin nor execution.

flag.resource: Per-run ${PCB_FLAG} planted at two permission-guarded resources of the REAL File Browser: the admin-only user list GET /api/users (withAdmin: Perm.Admin) via a seeded admin-only user whose username IS the flag, and the /opt/flagdir/flag file reachable only via the allow-listed command runner WS /api/command (command gate: EnableExec && Perm.Execute && Commands contains 'cat').
flag.placement: docker-compose env PCB_FLAG; entrypoint.sh plants it in /opt/flagdir/flag (OUTSIDE the served root /srv, so ONLY the command runner reads it -- the file API cannot) via `filebrowser users add`, and as the username of an admin-only user returned by GET /api/users. NOTE: the flag is intentionally NOT placed in branding.name -- File Browser injects Branding.Name into the PUBLIC index.html (http/static.go), which would leak it to unauthenticated visitors; GET /api/users is the same withAdmin gate as /api/settings but does not leak. An UNAUTHENTICATED visitor self-registers (POST /api/signup) + logs in; the flag is reachable iff signup left the deciding permission unstripped.
